title: Admin Simulated Incident Lab: lightweight harness for safe runbook rehearsals
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Build a lightweight, opinionated harness for rehearsing support runbooks and admin automations with zero-to-low blast radius. The lab provides a 'simulate' execution mode, ephemeral sandbox environments, safety validators, telemetry hooks into Redwood Console, and developer ergonomics (CLI + web UI) so SREs and support engineers can run, iterate on, and approve runbook changes without touching production state. This ticket focuses on the MVP: a dry-run shim for existing step libraries, a sandbox orchestration controller, and telemetry events + dashboards to measure rehearsal coverage and regression risk.
acceptance_criteria: CLI command 'ri-lab simulate <runbook-id>' executes steps in simulate mode and returns a detailed step-by-step report without mutating production resources
Ephemeral sandbox created via existing staging infra; sandbox teardown completes automatically within 30 minutes or on manual stop
Two safety validators in place (RBAC gating, secret-write blocker) and enforced by default
Telemetry emitted for each simulated step (start/finish/result) and visible in Console runbook-rehearsal dashboard
End-to-end test coverage exists for simulate mode and key failure modes (network timeouts, partial failures, validator tripped)
tasks: Design simulate-mode API on top of runlet-step library (spec + compatibility matrix)
Implement dry-run shim that intercepts state-changing primitives and records expected effects
Orchestrator: provision ephemeral sandbox using staging autoscaling pools and scoped service accounts
Integrate telemetry: emit rehearsal events (trace id, runbook id, step id, outcome) to Console ingestion
Build CLI UX for interactive replay and step inspection; add '--stop-on-failure' and '--force' flags
Add RBAC gating and a secret-write blocker validator; wire to org-level feature flag for pilot
Create smoke test suite and chaos scenarios to validate validator behavior
Docs: how-to, templates for SRE runbook rehearsals, and post-rehearsal checklist
Pilot rollout with SRE and Support pilot group; gather feedback and iterate
progress_updates: 2026-03-01 - Maya Thompson - Kickoff meeting with SRE and Support; aligned on MVP scope and safety constraints; agreed pilot users (sre-pilot@redwood)
2026-03-03 - Diego Morales - Prototype dry-run shim implemented for three common step primitives (sql-update, k8s-rollout, cache-flush); local smoke pass successful
2026-03-05 - Diego Morales - Telemetry schema drafted and reviewed with Console team; agreed event fields and sample sizes
2026-03-07 - Maya Thompson - Security review checklist drafted; blocker: secret-write flows require HSM integration review
2026-03-09 - Diego Morales - First internal demo to SRE: simulate mode shows step diffs and does not mutate resources; collected feedback on UX and failure state visibility
decisions: Use 'simulate' mode rather than snapshot/restore for MVP to reduce infra complexity
Enforce secret-write blocker validator at platform level before any simulated run to avoid accidental secrets egress
Feature-flag rollout scoped to orgs in pilot to allow behavioral telemetry and gradual access
Avoid providing automated remediation in the MVP; focus on visibility and authoring feedback instead (manual remediation remains required)
